items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: But my heart was set on going with Bashe and Tommy. In fact, we would have rehearsals every day

ctx.x: We were talking about the Savoy...

Yeah, they were working at the Savoy then. So I just got in town, well, actually, they're the first ones that knew I was back and whatnot. They told me their program, and they were working up there and everything. So they say, I never belonged to the New York local, you know. In fact, at that time, I was under the impression I didn't belong to any local because I hadn't paid any dues in Chicago for a period of five years, four or five years. So they say, well, we've got to arrange it, we've got to smuggle you in…
They said, no, you're still originally a member of Chicago.

items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Tommy got back before I did, and he and Bashir had formed this band, the New Orleans Feet Warmers, you know. So they greeted me with welcome arms in New York.

ctx.x: Chicago here, and so when I finally come back to New York, well Tommy got back before I did, and he and Bashir had formed this band, the New Orleans Feet Warmers, you know. So they greeted me with welcome arms in New York. They were working at the Savoy, and they had six pieces of terrific bands, so they wanted me, and he fit right in. But I made one fatal mistake, which cost me quite a bit of career-wise. I was so anxious and so overjoyed to be back home and to see old friends. There was, at that time, they were…
